title: Salt That Never Stops Forming
logline: In shallow coastal pans salt forms, is raked away and forms again within days, a heap that always looks the same because it is never the same crystal twice.
human_question: What does it mean for something to look unchanged, when every part of it is quietly being replaced?

situation.what_happens: Workers flood shallow pans, let them evaporate, rake what forms and carry it to a heap, then start again. The cycle takes days and repeats through a season. The heap beside the pans stays roughly the same size for months while almost nothing in it is what was there before. The work is physically severe, the pay is tied to weight, and one unseasonal rain can dissolve a week of it.
situation.who_is_involved: The workers, usually paid by what they gather and working in sun, brine and glare; whoever holds the lease on the pans and sells the output; and buyers whose prices move with a season that everyone else is at the mercy of.
situation.what_is_at_stake: A season's earnings against weather nobody controls, and the physical cost of the work on the people doing it, which is cumulative and rarely discussed. For the operation, whether the season closes at a price worth the labour.
situation.how_it_unfolds: A season begins when the weather allows and ends when it stops allowing. The pressures are rain, heat, labour and the price. It ends with a harvest gathered, a harvest lost, or a season cut short, and the weather decides, not the film.

concept_merge.why_together: C039 contributes the claim this film exists for: things look unchanged not because they are still but because their parts do not all break at once and each one that goes is replaced in the same place, so stability is constant, well-timed renewal. C037 contributes the join that makes the film more than a landscape, since the sources hold that every moment of mind rests on a piece of living matter, and that matter is made of exactly the stuff C039 has just described as constantly replaced. C042 contributes the three-beat shape both of them share, arising, standing and dissolving, which the charts draw as three dots because a mind's version of it is too fast to see. A salt pan is one of the few places where that three-beat shape happens slowly enough to be watched.
concept_merge.what_it_reveals: On its own C039 is a claim about a scale nobody can reach. Set beside a heap that is rebuilt every few days by people whose bodies are wearing out at a slower version of the same rate, it becomes something a viewer can hold: the worker, the heap and the pan are the same kind of fact at three different speeds. What the pair must not be allowed to become is a lesson about impermanence, which the digest notes neither source draws here.

concept_links.why: The digest gives the source's account of matter's lifespan, seventeen mind-moments or fifty-one sub-moments with a long standing phase, and Margaya's explanation of why objects still seem to last for months: like a sand heap seen from a distance, everything is a cluster of countless tiny units that do not all break at once, and each one that breaks is replaced in the same spot [C039-M:L9]. A season in a salt pan is a working match for that claim. The digest's limits are carried without exception: the clusters are not atoms, molecules or cells; seventeen mind-moments is not a duration in seconds and 'less than a hundred-thousandth of an eye-blink' is an image rather than a figure to quote as science; the source draws no moral about letting go here, and the film draws none either; and the replacement argument must never be paired with 'you are a new person every seven years'.

Re-grounded. The digest says that for beings with both mind and body no mental event floats free: each one happens somewhere and rests on a particular piece of living body, and when the body changes, what the mind can do changes with it [C037-P:L27]. The join with C039 is the point, and it is what this episode's lesson cites: the base a mind leans on is itself made of the material that C039 has just described as continuously replaced, so the support is being rebuilt underneath the thing it supports. The digest's prohibitions are carried: the heart-base is not cardiology and not 'follow your heart', 'beings with complete faculties' must never become a judgement about disabled people, and the digest's own candour that Margaya says this base cannot be found by medicine is stated plainly rather than smoothed over.

Re-grounded. The previous reading treated the pans' work cycle as an echo of the sources' notation for a fast process, which the notation is not. What the digest actually supports is narrower and better: the charts draw every single moment as three dots, arising, standing and dissolving, because that rhythm is shared by mind and matter and differs only in how long the middle beat lasts [C042-M:L3]. A pan is the rare case where a material thing's arising, standing and dissolving runs slowly enough to be watched, so it is the scale analogue of what the charts stand in for. This is stated in the film as a comparison of scale, never as a claim that a salt pan shows mind-moments, and the digest's rule that the charts are not readouts and must not be animated as such is observed.

what_the_viewer_could_understand: A heap of salt can look the same all season while every grain in it is new. These texts describe solid things the same way: countless tiny parts that each last a moment and are constantly replaced, so the whole seems not to change, and the body a mind rests on is made of the same replaced stuff.
what_must_be_real: The workers' real pay, conditions and physical cost. No time-lapse or montage may aestheticise the labour away, and the season's real economics belong in the film alongside the cycle. The sources' figures are never offered as measurements or as science.
position_hint: opening candidate for the group's early stretch: it establishes that the things the senses meet are brief and continuously replaced, which every later film in the group depends on, and it does so at the only speed a camera can actually hold. No location reasoning is involved.
risks: Time-lapse or montage treatment aestheticising the labour away.
Pay and conditions glossed over for a landscape film.
Weather dependency making a full cycle hard to film.
Presenting the source's replacement argument as cell turnover or physics, which the digest rules out.
Letting the film drift into a lesson about impermanence, which neither source draws here.
drop_if: No operation allows filming across a real working cycle.
The workers do not want their economic situation shown alongside the visual cycle.
Weather or access make a full cycle impossible to film.
The only available version of the work is mechanised in a way that removes the human cost the film is partly about.

connections.note: Both watch a material that seems constant and a trade built on judging it, one renewed every few days and one that has been there for an age.
Two ways of holding something too fast to watch: a notation that stands in for it, and a material slow enough to watch instead.

selection.reason: Used by EPD-0037, proposed by the C039 digest's own story seed, and now carrying re-grounded C037 and C042 links instead of the loose ones it had.

unknowns: No participant or event has been found or confirmed. Everything here is a research direction.
